# Transformer Attention & Scaled Dot-Product Attention in NumPy

## The Core Idea

In a Transformer, every token in a sequence can "attend to" every other token. Instead of processing tokens sequentially (as in RNNs), the model computes, for each position, a weighted combination of all positions. Those weights come from a simple dot-product similarity between learned **queries** and **keys**, and the values being combined are the **values** themselves.

### The Three Roles

| Matrix | Shape | Role | Analogy |
|--------|-------|------|---------|
| **Q** (Queries) | `(seq, d_k)` | "What am I looking for?" | Search query |
| **K** (Keys) | `(seq, d_k)` | "What do I contain?" | Document title |
| **V** (Values) | `(seq, d_v)` | "What is my actual content?" | Document body |

Each is produced by a learned linear projection of the input embedding:

```
Q = X · W_Q      K = X · W_K      V = X · W_V
```

### The Formula

$$
\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) \;=\; \text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) V
$$

Step by step:

1. **Score** — `Q @ K.T`
